title: The Secret to Overcoming Tech Resistance: It’s Not What You Think
author: Colette Molteni
summary: Colette Molteni argues that teams resist new technology not because of its features but because the people rolling it out move to the sale before understanding stakeholder needs. Drawing on her experience in analytics, she lays out an emotional-intelligence approach to change: lead with pain points, ask non-leading questions, speak the stakeholder's language, and confirm alignment before proposing solutions. A personal story of talking past a manager about two similar-sounding terms shows how misunderstanding erodes trust. Her closing formula is trust first, tech second. The piece is written for technical professionals but its lessons apply to any leader introducing change.
points: Selling too soon fails because it ignores the concerns of the Late Majority, who need their needs addressed before any pitch.
Surface pain points by asking open, non-leading questions and holding back solutions until the problems are clearly established.
Check that both parties mean the same thing by key terms, since hidden misalignment undermines trust.
Rejection of new tech is usually about perceived irrelevance to real problems, not about feature gaps.
Resistance to change is human and normal, so empathy-led rollout steps can turn it into adoption.
quotes: It's not about you, it is about them. Focus on them first, then address your needs.

The challenge here is not just to listen but to guide the conversation to get them to talk even more. Ask questions without leading. Veer them away from the solution until the end, when you have the pain points established.
Check for understanding and make sure you are aligned. This is good relationship management, reduces friction, and builds trust.
A smooth rollout is built upon addressing the needs and concerns of stakeholders first. Pain points come first, and then solutions to resolve them follow.
Resistance to new tech is common. We are human and tend to hate change, even good change. With the right steps, you can master this, shatter the resistance, and drive impactful change.
